scope: Implementation test oracles, not executed proofs

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Every new-format table MUST have one ordered map from typed primary key to stored row value, bound to a stable table/schema identity.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Table lookup/order MUST use the language's logical key comparison, not filename order, CBOR byte order or hash order.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The canonical page/group algorithm, encoding and bounds MUST be those in ORP-1; runtime optimizations MUST produce identical canonical output for the same logical snapshot.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Blob fields MUST use small annotated-content references in stored rows; media bytes MUST never be expanded into row-page bytes or base64 row text.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-005
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Large rows/strings/collections MUST use the shared value-overflow graph so metadata pages and direct dependency fanout remain bounded.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-006
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Copy-on-write updates MUST reuse unchanged nodes where canonical boundaries permit it; changed indices and payload bytes MUST be measured separately.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-007
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Partial fetch MUST preserve exact schema/root pins and return unavailable rather than empty/successfully truncated results on missing objects.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-008
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Secondary indexes and long-key VFS name indexes MUST use the same ordered store profile and commit atomically with the rows they index.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-009
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: An unindexed scan MAY require broad reads; explain/counters MUST distinguish estimated from actual transfer, decode and scan work.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-010
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Page rewrites/repacking/rechunking MUST NOT produce logical mutations when decoded values/annotations are unchanged.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-011
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Mutation/assertion/reference validation MUST be shared across all entrypoints; no VFS-specific weaker rules are permitted.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-012
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Raw storage nodes MUST not be exposed as writable row files; external graph modification requires full admission before use.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-013
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Format-1/2 histories MUST retain versioned readers. Migration MUST NOT dual-write the old row layouts or silently upgrade a historical commit.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-014
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: New `sys.Storage` metadata MUST describe root, schema, generation, row count when known, and observed bytes/availability; removed preference/placement modes MUST NOT survive as hidden toggles.

scenarios.title: row store: ORNA-ROW-015
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The native graph MUST connect all direct dependencies through real Git tree entries, use one object store, and reject mismatching, unused or type-invalid dependency edges.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Each nonterminal node MUST be an ordinary Git tree with `data` and optional `refs`; `data` is one canonical bounded CBOR blob and `refs` maps native OID names to exact child object types.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The direct dependency inventory in decoded data MUST exactly match `refs`, deduplicated by OID; missing, unused, malformed or wrong-type edges MUST be rejected.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Terminal binary chunks MUST be raw Git blobs. No separate media server, pointer-only object or second hash warehouse is permitted.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Node metadata MUST be at most 64 KiB and direct fanout at most 256; larger values/indices MUST use the same bounded graph recursively.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-005
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Objects MUST be validated under their format, schema and context before use. A shared child MUST NOT bypass per-parent semantic constraints.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-006
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Git SHA-1 and SHA-256 modes MUST retain native OID widths and verification; neither native OID equals the raw-content SHA-256 by definition.

scenarios.title: native reachability: ORNA-GRAPH-007
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The store root MUST contain only snapshot-required reachable state. Retained history belongs to ancestry/pins, not a current-root catalogue of every historical object.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Blob MUST represent a finite octet sequence with canonical media type and optional suffix hint. The metadata MUST NOT alter the raw-byte content commitment.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: This release MUST NOT add intrinsic `File`, `Asset`, `Bytes` or `Clob` synonyms or mandatory tables. Existing `sys.File` source-catalogue objects remain distinct from media values.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Blob MUST work in ordinary stored/nested values; Blob primary keys remain inadmissible.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Content identity MUST be `(length, SHA256(raw bytes))`, independent of MIME, suffix, Git object header/algorithm, compression, chunking, path and snapshot.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-005
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Blob value equality MUST compare canonical annotations and exact content. `same_content` ignores annotations. Equal digests MUST NOT override detected unequal bytes; independently supplied equal-digest content without a shared admitted witness requires exact streamed comparison or explicit unavailability.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-006
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Detected content collisions MUST fail without overwriting or aliasing an existing content identity.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-007
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Loading a row, passing a same-database Blob reference, showing metadata, reading length/digest or changing MIME/title MUST NOT hydrate media just to form a `Vec<u8>`, encode a row or calculate its semantic digest.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-008
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Held values MUST retain their exact resolution context for their owner/pin lifetime; unavailable/expired values MUST NOT rebind through a later row or HEAD.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-009
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Structured portable annotated values MUST use negotiated OVB-2; old OVB-1 keeps its original bytes-only semantics. No implicit annotation-dropping or reference-in-byte-slot conversion is allowed.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-010
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Inspectors MUST display type, length, declaration and content commitment without payload dumps or remote analysis. The VFS/row representation MUST use small references, not base64 media.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-011
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: `read` MUST check nonnegative offsets/lengths, offset at/before EOF, checked arithmetic and at most 8 MiB per call; only known EOF clips a successful result.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-012
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Range acquisition MUST fetch required descriptors/intersecting chunks and only separately bounded read-ahead. Whole Git-object overfetch MUST be measured, not called exact range transfer.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-013
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: BlobWriter MUST be owner/runtime-bound and nonserializable, with open/finished/aborted states, serialized append/finish/abort, idempotent terminal outcomes and cancellation cleanup.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-014
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Begin/append/finish MUST enforce declared expected length, total quota and the format maximum 2^63−1. No unbounded buffer or temporary-file bypass is allowed.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-015
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Exact snapshot hydration MUST respect offline/network policy and cancellation; host `capture_file` is external I/O and remains forbidden in historical/pure/presenter/assertion contexts.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-016
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Format-3 row/argument/consumer semantic commitments MUST use the versioned SOV-3 domains, not Git layout OIDs or eager full-byte encodings.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-017
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Cross-format comparison MUST compare decoded values under explicit migration semantics, not unrelated digest bytes.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-018
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The existing live protocol MUST reject unnegotiated OVB-2/storage tags. Use typed safe inspector/reference responses and separately authorized content I/O, not automatic full-Blob result serialization.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-019
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Copying into an independent database MUST establish and protect destination closure before acknowledging a dependent row, with no hidden dependency on the original user's path.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-020
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Generic slicing/concatenation MUST produce octet-stream/null annotations unless it is an exact identity no-op; part of a JPEG does not automatically remain image/jpeg.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-BLOB-021
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Byte export MUST mean original raw bytes. Full annotated value export MUST preserve metadata explicitly; an export operation cannot silently switch between these two promises.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The root Blob descriptor MUST bind exact length, raw-byte SHA-256 and its native content graph. MIME and suffix MUST be stored with each referencing value, not as global facts about a hash.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Chunk entries MUST bind native object OID, byte length and independent chunk SHA-256; offset traversal MUST validate lengths, height and bounds.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Zero-length content MUST have one canonical empty descriptor; zero-length nonempty-index children, wrong total length and excessive height MUST be rejected.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Metadata-only access MUST not read chunks. Full verification MUST compare every chunk plus the complete raw-content digest before claiming full integrity.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-005
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The chosen partition rule MUST be reproducible; insertions and adversarial patterns MUST have explicit bounded-resource behaviour and measured index churn.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-006
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Native Git graph validation MUST not be replaced by checking a descriptor string. Missing promised data is unavailable; unknown missing data is corruption/incomplete closure.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-007
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: All newly persisted Blob fields MUST use reference form regardless of payload size. Small Blobs may use one terminal chunk, not a second inline-row mode.

scenarios.title: annotated/lazy content: ORNA-OGB-008
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Cross-representation equality and semantic diff MUST ignore rechunking, graph OIDs and Git repacking while retaining annotation changes.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Every new Blob MUST have a valid concrete declared MIME value; constructors without knowledge use application/octet-stream, never a wildcard or empty string.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Normalization MUST lowercase type/subtype/parameter names, sort parameters, normalize charset case, and preserve other case-sensitive parameter values; duplicate names, controls and malformed quoted strings MUST fail.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: A preferred suffix MUST be chosen from MIME-1 by essence; a compatible explicit safe hint overrides it, otherwise unknown types use bin.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Explicit hints MUST be lowercase safe ASCII suffix segments of at most 32 bytes, without leading dot, slash, backslash, empty segments or traversal. Known-type incompatible hints MUST fail.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-005
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Defaults matching the preferred suffix MUST canonicalize to no hint; normal spelling/quoting/case variations MUST not create different annotated values.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-006
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Import resolution MUST be explicit declaration first, then bounded trusted detection, then a uniquely mapped suffix, then octet-stream. Conflicting observations MUST be disclosed; host-specific MIME registries cannot silently decide persistent metadata.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-007
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Detection MUST NOT run on listings/stat/metadata-only edits. Unsupported or damaged content MUST remain preservable unless an explicit schema constraint requires a valid format.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-008
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: MIME changes MUST update projected filenames atomically while keeping existing content handles pinned. Renames do not transcode or grant executable status.

scenarios.title: canonical declaration and suffix: ORNA-MIME-009
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: HTML/SVG/JS previews MUST not execute merely because the stored declaration requests it. Trusted application assets and arbitrary user-content downloads require different explicit serving policies.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: A virtual row directory MUST address database/table/typed key; `data.orna` MUST encode stored non-key fields only, under that snapshot's schema.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Virtual row text and sibling content files MUST be projections of the shared row store, not materialized competing authoritative copies.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Unchanged schema-directed Blob references MUST resolve internally in the captured row/draft context without reopening the mount or reading payloads.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Relative paths MUST stay within that field's registered projection. Absolute paths, symlink/traversal escapes and implicit cross-row references MUST fail.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-005
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Commit selectors MUST pin one snapshot; a branch-name snapshot selector resolves once. Workspace mounts MUST share one selected worktree's durable CWD.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-006
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Every accepted edit MUST use normal transaction/assertion/reference/permission validation and never automatically create a Git commit.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-007
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: FUSE `release` MUST NOT be the only rejection/durability point; callback behavior and close-error limitations MUST be disclosed.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-008
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Dirty sequence capture and acceptance MUST serialize with writes; `dup`/fork/repeated flush MUST not create a second acceptance of the same candidate.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-009
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Invalid/stale candidates MUST preserve original accepted values, protect retained draft bytes and return a stable error/diagnostic association.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-010
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: A metadata-only save MUST not fetch or rehash sibling content. A binary save MAY require streaming the entire resulting bytes to establish its raw SHA-256; memory remains bounded.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-011
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Normal save CAS MUST compare the captured write/temp-create baseline. Strong initial-read protection MUST be claimed only for a retained edit token/guarded operation.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-012
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Renaming a suffix MUST not transcode bytes, rename columns or rekey a row. Compatible aliases update only the explicit suffix hint through CAS.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-013
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Removing a required Blob MUST fail; optional Blob unlink MAY set that field to null after validation. Deleting `data.orna` MUST fail; row deletion is an explicit database operation.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-014
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Hard links, device nodes, symlinks and writable shared mmap are unsupported in VFS-1 and MUST fail explicitly. Private mmap/read copies do not modify the database.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-015
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Multiple file saves MUST NOT be guessed into one transaction. `orna edit --row PATH` provides explicit grouped row/content admission; separate updates may reject cross-field constraints.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-016
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Reserved/colliding names MUST be escaped reversibly, not rejected as otherwise valid database keys or merged by case-folding.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-017
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Directory iteration MUST be lazy/paged and pinned; lookup of a known key MUST use the index. An exhaustive recursive scan can still fetch all requested data.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-018
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: `stat`, directory listings and row documents MUST not sniff/decode/download Blob content; raw-file size comes from the exact content descriptor.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-019
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Schema changes, MIME path changes and API writes MUST invalidate directory/attribute caches coherently. Existing handles MUST not retarget to a different row or reordered collection element.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-020
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Source files MAY be edited through the shared workspace source path; complete candidate validation and explicit grouped source edits are required when several files change together. No evaluation occurs during speculative file writes.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-021
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Sync/rename acknowledgement, new content pins, local row commitment and namespace recovery MUST be journalled so crashes cannot lose acknowledged content.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-022
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: FUSE writeback caching MUST be off initially; supported caching/IO modes MUST preserve per-open generation semantics despite non-VFS database writers.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-023
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: The adapter MUST NOT expose a fake `.git` directory or writable raw store. Git commands target the backing repository, never generated row documents.

scenarios.title: filesystem editing: ORNA-VFS-024
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Unmount MUST refuse dirty/unresolved accepted-state recovery unless an explicit policy retains it safely. It MUST NOT report discarded drafts as saved.

scenarios.title: capture and durability: ORNA-CAP-001
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Every acknowledged row containing new content MUST have durable verified new objects and native retention roots; a hash string in SQLite is insufficient.

scenarios.title: capture and durability: ORNA-CAP-002
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Inherited promised objects MAY remain unhydrated only with recorded snapshot/promisor evidence; newly imported unknown bytes MUST NOT be acknowledged as merely promised.

scenarios.title: capture and durability: ORNA-CAP-003
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
then: Runtime pin refs MUST be local, owner-scoped and excluded from ordinary remote push; export of unpublished work MUST first freeze a recoverable consistent root.

scenarios.title: capture and durability: ORNA-CAP-004
given: A disposable database using the final format and the actual production implementation.
when: Exercise the rule, its rejected inputs and the relevant concurrency/recovery boundary.
